visual_goal: Show the redesigned SFP subledger pipeline: producers publish business facts; only the accounting engine writes entries under an approved rule version and an open period; summarizer and tie-out make the GL posting a reconcilable boundary.
prompt: A left-to-right pipeline illustration. At the far left, three small producer boxes stacked vertically: 'Booking platform', 'Northmere Pay', 'Payout engine', each sending one lightning-bolt arrow into a horizontal pipe labeled 'Event backbone'. The pipe flows into a gate box labeled 'Intake'; from 'Intake' one small arrow drops down into a quarantine tray labeled 'Quarantine'. From 'Intake' one arrow into a tall stack labeled 'Event store'. Next, a large gear box labeled 'Accounting engine' receiving one arrow from 'Event store'; above it two small inputs feed down into it: a rulebook labeled 'Approved rules' and a plain calendar page with a green check mark, labeled 'Open period'. From the engine one arrow into an open book labeled 'Journal'. From the journal one arrow to a funnel labeled 'Summarizer', then one arrow to a box labeled 'S/4HANA GL', with exactly one thin dashed arrow curving back over the top from 'S/4HANA GL' to 'Summarizer'. Below, a balance scale labeled 'Tie-out' receives one arrow from 'Journal' and one from 'S/4HANA GL'.
alt: Booking, payment and payout producers publish events to a backbone; intake quarantines bad events and stores the rest; only the accounting engine, using approved rules and an open period, writes the journal; a summarizer posts to the S/4HANA GL and a tie-out weighs the journal against it.

visual_goal: Show that one event becomes one entry: rule selection uses business time, the period check uses the accounting date, and the posting key turns a duplicate delivery into a no-op returning the original entry.
prompt: A left-to-right flow illustration. At the far left two identical envelopes with a lightning bolt, one slightly behind the other, both labeled once 'PaymentCaptured e1', arriving at a gate box labeled 'Intake'. One arrow from 'Intake' into a large gear box labeled 'Accounting engine'. Above the engine, a rulebook labeled 'Rule version 2' with a small clock icon tagged 'business time', connected to the engine by one arrow down. Below the engine, a calendar labeled 'Period open' with a small tag 'accounting date', connected to the engine by one arrow up. From the engine one arrow right into an open book labeled 'Journal' containing one highlighted entry with a key icon labeled 'posting key'. A second, lighter arrow from the engine bounces off the key icon and curves back to the engine, labeled 'duplicate: same entry'.
alt: Two deliveries of the same PaymentCaptured event reach intake and the accounting engine, which picks the rule by business time and checks the period by accounting date, then writes one journal entry; the posting key turns the duplicate into a no-op returning the same entry.

visual_goal: Show SFP period states: standard postings only in Open, SoftClosed takes only approved adjustments, Closed and Locked take nothing, and reopening is an approved exception.
prompt: A left-to-right path of five rounded stepping stones: 'Future', 'Open', 'SoftClosed', 'Closed', 'Locked'. One arrow connects each stone to the next. Icons on the stones: an empty calendar page on 'Future'; an open door with many small document slips flowing in on 'Open'; a half-closed door with one slip carrying a check mark on 'SoftClosed'; a closed door on 'Closed'; a padlock on 'Locked'. Above the row, one short curved arrow arches from the top of 'SoftClosed' back to the top of its left neighbour 'Open'; this arch spans only those two adjacent stones. Below 'Closed' sits a smaller orange stone labeled 'Reopened' with a green check-mark seal icon; one arrow goes down from 'Closed' into 'Reopened' and one arrow goes back up from 'Reopened' into 'Closed'.
alt: Period states from Future to Open, SoftClosed, Closed and Locked; open periods take many postings, soft-closed only approved adjustments, closed and locked none; a soft-closed period can return to open, and a closed period can be reopened with approval and closed again.
